seasons.title: The Lake Counts
seasons.summary: Days 1-19. The lake went silent, warm and clear, and rose without rain. Lost pets came home wet, humming and slightly cold. Gerald Pith measured the water; Agnes Crewe, 91, who remembered the last waking, spoke in riddles. On Day 9 the whole town sat at the shore and the lake lit gently from below. It counted nine, was satisfied, and receded. The coda left a first sealed letter in the Gazette's lost-and-found.

seasons.title: The Correspondence
seasons.summary: Days 20-50. Sealed letters from 'H' arrived daily in the lost-and-found, addressed to people not yet in town (Oduya, Beaumont, Harrow) and to residents (Crane, Crewe). The shore ice crept in. Calloway arrived Day 35 as the dock froze; T. Aldercott, who shares the editor's surname and carries a typewriter, arrived Day 38. Calloway took over the library and its east alcove. Oduya, Beaumont and Harrow never came.

seasons.title: The Alcove
seasons.summary: Days 51-82. Green-cloth books began appearing in the library's east alcove, dated in the future and predicting the town's days. The editor named it an experiment (Day 63). On Day 65 Calloway answered aloud: 'We have decided to keep reading.' The books began to thank the town; the ninth listed the real census of nine. Agnes finally stated her law plainly (Day 75). A library card with a pocket calendar of stamps in many hands turned up behind the ninth book.

seasons.title: Sarah Voss
seasons.summary: Days 83-109. The pocket calendar kept stamping itself, each in a different hand. Doreen's loaf wandered to the empty Petrakis house; a line ran from the alcove to its kitchen. Doreen announced her retirement (Day 90) but kept baking. The Kettle's cups multiplied; a fifth chair filled. The stamps ended with a name, Sarah Voss, owed a chair for a book borrowed fourteen years ago. She walked in on Day 99 and borrowed a Bronte novel. The ice held and the town rested.

The strangeness jumped containers: Gerald's private phrase 'already spoken for' turned up chalked in an unfamiliar hand on Hank Mossley's locked hardware-store board, proving the phenomenon is no longer tied to one person or one porch, and Toby logged it as the sequence's first entry found away from the green house.
